name: @corbits-builder/digitalocean
description: Publishes the project's app to a server Builder makes for the person in their own DigitalOcean account, so people can open it at the server's address.
author: Sawyer Cutler <sawyer@dirtroad.dev>

builder.when: The person wants their app published to, checked on or taken off a server at DigitalOcean that Builder makes for them in their own DigitalOcean account, so people can open it at the server's address.
builder.unless: The project has no saved app yet, the person wants it published somewhere other than DigitalOcean, or they already rent a server of their own to publish to.

digitalocean.choice.about: The server the person agreed to rent at DigitalOcean, as { "size": DigitalOcean's name for its size, "region": where it runs, "monthly": the monthly price in US dollars they were shown, "team": { "id", "name" } of the DigitalOcean team that pays, "at": when they agreed, as an ISO time }; none once the server it was for is gone, so a new one needs a new answer. Only the Publish to DigitalOcean screen saves it, and only DigitalOcean's own tools clear it.

digitalocean.quote.about: The monthly price DigitalOcean asked for a size when it differed from the one the person was shown, as { "size", "monthly" }, so the Publish to DigitalOcean screen shows the real price when opened again. Only DigitalOcean's own tools save it.

digitalocean.server.about: DigitalOcean's tools' own note of the server Builder makes there, as { "stage": creating while a create is under way, bound once Builder's key works on it, "id" at DigitalOcean once known, "address" once bound, "label": its name there, "team": { "id", "name" } of the DigitalOcean team it is made under, "attempts": servers made for the choice agreed at "for" }; with no stage, nothing is made and only the tries are kept; none once the server is gone. Only DigitalOcean's own tools save it.

digitalocean-server.about: the key to your server at DigitalOcean

publisher.label: Publisher
publisher.hint: Publishes the app where the person chose and explains what went wrong.

facts.ready:digitalocean: the saved app says how it runs in production, as a publish to a server at DigitalOcean needs
facts.published:digitalocean: the app as saved now is published on the person's server at DigitalOcean
facts.removable:digitalocean: the person agreed, on the take-down screen, to delete the server at DigitalOcean with the app as it is published or held there now

examples: publish the app to a DigitalOcean droplet
is my app still up on DigitalOcean
take the app off DigitalOcean and delete the server
